Same mechanism as the review page - the browser's print dialogue, with outcome-testing.css's print rules stripping the chrome - so the two exports cannot drift apart. Offered only once at least one review on the case has been SUBMITTED, which is the same test the review page now applies to its own button. It used to be enough that a review instance existed. That put the export on a case whose checks were still being answered, and the file it produced was a draft with no submission date on it - indistinguishable, once printed, from the record of a finished check. It is not one of the numbered issues and is no longer raised as one: it is the result every issue in the table is a reason for, and numbering it among them read as one more thing the adviser had to put right (project owner, 2026-09-10). Remediation.Describe writes it in brackets at the end of the standing sentence - "...when the review was submitted (Tax check: Insufficient evidence)." - so it is already on every action and needs no column of its own. The marker has to be there before the brackets mean anything: an action raised with no reason behind it still carries the sentence, and a checker's observation is free text that may have brackets of its own. Once it is, the outcome is the last bracket the description opens, the observation being written above the sentence and never below it. Both splits are on one character, this Liquid having no multi-character split, and each is assigned before it is walked, a for tag taking a variable rather than a filtered expression. The two ends are taken by walking the pieces rather than with first / last or an index - the same caution the item split below is written with, on a site that has rejected both an index into a collection and a two-argument filter. Read across every action rather than off the first, so a case whose Tax and AQS reviews both raised remediation names both. Each record keeps it so it stands alone in Dataverse; the table shows it once per run of actions that share it, rather than under every row. {% endcomment %} {% assign ot_shown_note = '' %} {% for a in case_actions %} {% assign latest = null %} {% for s in case_signoffs.results.entities %}{% if latest == null and s.al_remediationactionid.id == a.al_remediationactionid %}{% assign latest = s %}{% endif %}{% endfor %} {% if latest %} {% if latest.al_signoffdecision.value == 120910721 %}{% assign any_rejected = true %}{% assign all_approved = false %}{% endif %} {% else %} {% assign all_approved = false %} {% endif %} {% if form_source == null and a.al_clientcontactrequired %}{% assign form_source = a %}{% endif %} {% comment %} al_description carries the whole list Remediation.Describe built: a heading, one "- item" line per thing the checker marked down, then the checker's observation and the standing sentence. The agreed form numbers those items one to a row, so they are split back out here and the rest is shown once, under them. The standing sentence is dropped rather than shown: it said the same thing under every row of every case, and both halves of it are on the page in their own right now - the outcome as the remediation's Outcome above, and what to do about it as the row the adviser answers (project owner, 2026-09-10). It stays in al_description, which is the record Dataverse keeps and the only place the outcome is written down. Every filter used is one this site already relies on elsewhere, and the arguments are the shapes it already passes: no two-argument truncate and no multi-character split, both of which this Liquid rejects. The line break is turned into a single character first (newline_to_br writes a tag this Liquid understands whatever the stored line endings are) so the split is on one character. A line is an item when putting "- " back in front of it with its first "- " removed reproduces it - true only when the "- " was at the front, so "AML - No CRA" is an item's text, not a bullet. If any of that does not take, ot_count stays 0 and the action falls back to the single row it drew before. Inline rather than in a snippet of its own: an included template gets its own scope, so these assigns would not come back.
